nj_r_benes.blurb: Benes is a small top-rope cliff in the Cranberry Hollow cluster of northwest New Jersey. It has 19 top-rope lines, roughly 30 to 45 feet tall, on near-vertical, featured rock. Grades begin around 5.5 and 5.6, bunch up at 5.8 and 5.9, and reach a single 5.11, which makes it a decent place for newer climbers to log mileage on a rope. The wall faces southwest and mature trees shade much of it, so cool afternoons suit it best. Expect brush, slick holds, some loose rock and a damp, buggy base. Top anchors are set by scrambling up the slippery left side.

nj_parsippany_rock_house.blurb: Parsippany Rock House is a compact boulder spot in the Parsippany area of Morris County, tucked at the end of Dale Road. Enormous glacial boulders lean together to form a natural shelter that locals have known for generations. There are 19 bouldering problems here, most of them easy to moderate: V0 through V3 make up the bulk, with V1 the most common grade, and just one problem each at V4 and V5. The approach is practically nonexistent, so it works as a short stop for a quick session rather than a full day out, and it pairs naturally with other North Central New Jersey bouldering.

nj_garrett_mountain.blurb: Garrett Mountain is a bouldering zone on the crest of the First Watchung Mountain, within the Paterson and Woodland Park reservation in Passaic County. The problems sit just under a 50-foot tower on the ridgeline above Paterson, among arêtes, flakes and a splitter crack on the northwest corner. There are 17 problems, mostly V1 to V5, with a V0 warm-up at the easy end and one V8 at the top. The boulders are in the woods and partly hidden from view down the slope, so expect a quiet, low-key session close to the city.

nj_southfield.blurb: Southfield is one of the boulder zones in Sourland Mountain Preserve, on the Somerset County side near Hillsborough. The blocks sit on a steep, wooded hillside right beside a trail, away from the busier parts of the preserve, so it tends to be quiet. It has 15 problems, and the grades lean easy: six at V0, a spread of V1 to V3 problems, and a single V6 for the strong. That makes it a good fit for beginners and for climbers looking to string together a relaxed circuit. Combine it with the preserve's other boulder areas for a bigger day.

nj_cedar_grove_reservoir.blurb: Cedar Grove Reservoir is a small bouldering spot in Essex County, set among trees in a residential park. It is a place for local training rather than a trip destination. Four short walls, a trail wall, a near wall, a second wall and a back wall, hold 15 problems, and they are mostly very easy: ten sit at V0, with a handful at VB, V1 and V2. The boulders lie on both sides of a trail near a small hill, about a ten-minute walk from the parking area. It suits beginners, warm-ups and kids more than anyone chasing difficulty.
